chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: We were informed by Muhammad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, who said: Ahmad ibn Mitham al-Talhi narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Where was the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) buried? He said: 'He was buried in the grave of his father, Noah (peace be upon him).' I said: And where is the grave of Noah? The people say that it is in the Mosque. He said: 'No, that is in the rear of Kufa.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Where is the grave of Imam Ali located according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise location of Imam Ali’s tomb by distinguishing it from the general mosque complex, placing it specifically in the rear of Kufa near the grave of Noah. This distinction is significant in Shia tradition for validating the authenticity of the shrine and correcting popular misconceptions about its exact boundaries. The reference to Noah highlights the continuity of prophetic lineage and the sacred geography associated with the Ahl al-Bayt.
